item.title: Aaron Dessner Sets the Record Straight on Gracie Abrams’ ‘Death Wish’: It’s ‘Definitely Not’ About Taylor Swift
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're talking about Gracie Abrams' new album, "Daughter From Hell", and the story behind one of its most talked-about tracks, "Death Wish".
[Music transition]
Host: Gracie Abrams and producer Aaron Dessner have collaborated on three albums together, and their latest effort has sparked some interesting conversations. Specifically, around the song "Death Wish". Some fans have been wondering why the studio version sounds so different from the live piano version Gracie initially released. Aaron Dessner recently clarified the situation with Billboard.
[Audio clip of Aaron Dessner] Aaron Dessner: "The studio version predates the live recording by several months. We wrote it, actually, the week that we recorded other songs that were on 'The Secret of Us' deluxe. In the wake of 'Daughter From Hell' coming out, people were like, 'Wait, what about the original version?' This is the original version."
Host: So, it seems the studio version is actually the original. But what about the speculation that "Death Wish" is about Taylor Swift? Aaron Dessner sets the record straight.
[Audio clip of Aaron Dessner] Aaron Dessner: "Yeah, definitely not. It was written at a time when Gracie was writing about a friend's ex, being in a bad relationship. So it was kind of about that person, I think."
Host: It's clear that the song's meaning has been misunderstood. Aaron Dessner also shared that he and Gracie Abrams have a close relationship, and while they do discuss their personal lives, they don't always dive into the specifics of their songwriting.
[Music transition]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in to our conversation about Gracie Abrams' new album and the story behind "Death Wish". Join us next time for more music news and updates.
[Outro music plays]
